challengeTypes: identify: What is a LINE SEGMENT? (A straight path between two fixed endpoints with a definite length vs A straight path that extends forever in both directions vs A flat surface that extends forever)

sort: Drag each geometric term to its correct description (Point: a tiny dot showing position, no length | Line segment: straight path between two endpoints, definite length | Line: straight path extending infinitely both ways | Ray: starts at one point, extends infinitely one way | Plane: flat surface extending endlessly)
identify: What are PARALLEL lines? (Two straight lines that never meet, always the same distance apart vs Two lines that cross at one point vs Two lines that form a right angle)

sort: Drag each pair of lines to Parallel, Intersecting, or Perpendicular (Parallel: railway tracks, opposite sides of a ruler | Intersecting: two roads crossing, scissors blades | Perpendicular: wall and floor, plus sign lines)

extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Plane, point, line, line segment, ray, parallel — plane: flat surface extending endlessly (table top, blackboard). Point: tiny dot showing position, no length/width. Line segment: straight path between two endpoints, definite length (edge of textbook). Line: straight path extending infinitely both ways, no endpoints (railway track). Ray: starts at one point, extends infinitely one way (torch beam). Parallel lines: two lines that never meet, always same distance apart (railway tracks). (2) Intersecting and perpendicular lines — intersecting: two lines that cross at one point (two roads crossing). Perpendicular: intersecting lines that form a right angle (90 degrees) (wall and floor, plus sign). (3) Unit conversions — length: 1 metre = 100 cm. 3 m = 300 cm. 250 cm = 2 m 50 cm. mass: 1 kg = 1000 g. 2 kg = 2000 g. 1500 g = 1 kg 500 g. capacity: 1 litre = 1000 mL. 3 L = 3000 mL. Like rupees and paise: 1 rupee = 100 paise. (4) Daily-life problems — measuring length of cloth in metres, weighing vegetables in kg, measuring milk in litres. Choose the right unit for each measurement. (5) Estimation — estimate before measuring: pencil about 15 cm, door about 2 m, apple about 150 g, water bottle about 1 L, brick about 2 kg, classroom about 8 m. Verify by actual measurement. Misconceptions: 'a line and a line segment are the same' (a line extends infinitely both ways with NO endpoints, a line segment has TWO endpoints and a definite length), 'a ray extends in both directions' (a ray has ONE endpoint and extends in only ONE direction), 'parallel lines eventually meet' (parallel lines NEVER meet — they stay the same distance apart forever), '1 kg = 100 g' (1 kg = 1000 g, not 100 g — there are 1000 grams in a kilogram), 'perpendicular lines are the same as parallel lines' (perpendicular lines CROSS at 90 degrees, parallel lines never cross). Default width=720, height=560. Use named export (export function LinesMeasurementGame), NOT export default. Export interface LinesMeasurementGameProps with width?, height?, onComplete?: (score: number) => void. Use double quotes for ALL strings containing apostrophes. Use 'currentChallenge' as variable name, NOT 'challenge'. Auto-hint timer MUST be exactly 10000ms.
